title: AI Hackers Just Let Software Attack 100+ Websites—Could Your Next Security Breach Be Fully Automated?

lines.text: AI hasn't made hacking magic, it has made trying again almost free.
lines.label: TRY AGAIN

lines.text: Because Reuters found one operator whose AI agents did most of the work,
lines.label: REUTERS

lines.text: reaching more than one thousand two hundred websites
lines.label: 1,200+ SITES

lines.text: at over one hundred companies, with little human help.
lines.label: 100+ COMPANIES

lines.text: Now, reaching a site isn't breaking in, and the report doesn't say what was stolen.
But the agents hunted for weak points, wrote code and tested it.
lines.label: HUNT, WRITE, TEST

lines.text: That works through a feedback loop,
lines.label: FEEDBACK LOOP

lines.text: which means the agent tries a login, reads the error, changes one thing and tries again,
far more often than any person could.
So forgotten support pages and old control panels become the target,
lines.label: FORGOTTEN PAGES

lines.text: and one weak page can steal your login or change what you pay at checkout.
Still, nobody can show that AI attackers always win,
because defenders can run the same loop and patch old software every day.
lines.label: SAME LOOP

lines.text: And follow the channel, because the next one shows how defenders keep up.
Which leaves one question, should small businesses let AI guard their websites, yes or no?
